name: com.bliahub/blia-catalogue
title: BLIA — Bank Product Terms
description: Bank account terms as banks publish them, dated: fees, waivers, offers. Read-only. Canada today.

tools.name: list_coverage
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which banks, account types or provinces BLIA covers, how many accounts it holds, or when it was last updated -- or before saying BLIA does not cover something. No arguments. Returns each covered bank with its product classes, product and variant counts and provinces; the product classes covered and not covered; the kinds of information not covered; and last_update (when the snapshot was built and when a bank source was last read). A bank, class or province not listed is outside BLIA's snapshot, which says nothing about whether the bank offers it. For the accounts themselves use list_bank_products.

tools.name: list_bank_products
tools.description: Use this first when the user asks about Canadian bank accounts (currently chequing at the banks listed in coverage), or which accounts a bank offers. Returns every product in BLIA's snapshot with its product_slug, its variants (customer groups such as seniors, each with its eligibility note), the attributes published, and completeness, and per variant its monthly fee and its waiver (status, kind, the lowest balance that removes the whole fee, and the waiver rule's full summary), so one call lists every account's fee and waiver. A waivable fee is not a zero fee; no waiver is applied to the customer's balances. max_monthly_fee and waiver_kind filter on the variant cohort chooses (default current); an unpublished fee never matches and is counted. coverage says what BLIA does and does not cover; an empty result always says why. Filters combine. Pages hold up to 50 products; pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page (null on the last). Returns published values; source citations are not included. For a waiver's logic and every other term, take a product_slug from here to get_product_terms or compare_products.

institution.description: Institution id as listed in coverage.institutions_covered (bmo, cibc, rbc, scotia, td: the Big 5); a common or legal name such as BMO, RBC, Scotiabank or Royal Bank of Canada also resolves. Omit for all.

product_class.description: Product class. Only "chequing" is covered today.

province.description: Province: a two-letter code (ON, QC, ...) or a name such as Ontario or Québec; omit for all provinces.

cursor.description: product_slug returned as next_cursor by a prior call

max_monthly_fee.description: Optional, CAD: only products whose chosen variant (see cohort) has a published monthly fee at or under this, before any waiver. A fee BLIA has not published never matches and is counted in filters_applied.fee_unknown_excluded: unknown, not free.

waiver_kind.description: Optional: only products whose chosen variant's waiver kind is one of these (balance: money thresholds; relationship: other products or a programme; mixed; none: no waiver stated; not_published).

cohort.description: Customer group the terms apply to. Default "current" (the standard offer). Other groups a product carries (e.g. "senior_60_plus") are listed per product as variants; pass one to get that group's terms. Case and punctuation are ignored.

tools.name: get_product_terms
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one account's fees, included transactions, minimum balance, fee waiver conditions, e-transfer or ATM costs, or deposit insurance. Returns each published term with its value and effective date; a rule comes with its plain-language summary AND its logic (default outcome plus conditions with thresholds, e.g. the balance that waives the monthly fee). Says which customer-group variant was used, which others exist, which questions the terms answer (answerability) and exactly what is not published (before_acting). cohort, province and channel pick the variant (defaults current, ALL and any, echoed in defaults_applied; cohort ignores case and punctuation, so "Senior 60+" finds senior_60_plus). If none matches, no_variant_matched lists available_cohorts: a problem with the query, not missing data. A common variant of a published slug (the bank's full name, a trailing -account) answers for that product and is stated in defaults_applied; any other unknown product_slug returns an error naming the nearest published slugs, if any. not_published and unresolved mean unknown, never zero. Returns published values; source citations are not included. For several accounts side by side use compare_products; for perks or welcome offers across accounts use list_benefits or list_offers. as_of (YYYY-MM-DD) answers for a past date from the rows BLIA holds, each with its effective dates and whether the bank stated them; before BLIA's earliest record it says no_record_before. BLIA cannot say what a fee will be. Naming attributes returns those only: welcome offers are then counted in offers_withheld (never 'none'), and include=["offers"] returns them. Offers come without their clause ledger (counted in clauses_withheld); include=["clauses"] adds it.

product_slug.description: A product_slug from list_bank_products, e.g. td-every-day-chequing-account

province.description: Province: a two-letter code (ON, QC, ...) or a name such as Ontario or Québec. Default "ALL".

cohort.description: Customer group the terms apply to. Default "current" (the standard offer). Other groups a product carries (e.g. "senior_60_plus") are listed per product as variants; pass one to get that group's terms. Case and punctuation are ignored.

channel.description: How the account is opened. Default "any" (terms that apply whatever the channel).

attributes.description: Limit to these attributes (at most 40), e.g. monthly_fee, transaction_limit, minimum_balance, nsf_fee, etransfer_rules, atm_rules. Omit for all.

as_of.description: Optional past date, YYYY-MM-DD: the terms in force that day, e.g. the day a mortgage funded. A date before BLIA's earliest record answers no_record_before, never a value. Omit for today's terms.

include.description: With attributes named, welcome offers are left out and counted in offers_withheld; "offers" returns them too. Without attributes all terms, benefits and offers are returned. Each offer's clause ledger is left out and counted in clauses_withheld; "clauses" returns it.

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to compare accounts, within one bank or across banks. One call returns, for each product: monthly fee, annual fee before waivers, included transactions (checked against monthly_transactions if given), minimum balance, NSF fee, the fee-waiver conditions (summary and logic), e-transfer and ATM terms, and what is missing -- plus a ranking by monthly fee with the annual difference to the lowest. It never applies a waiver to the customer's balances: it gives the conditions so they can be checked. Products whose fee BLIA has not published are listed as not_ranked, never ranked as free. The ranking uses published monthly fee and nothing else: monthly_transactions adds a separate ranking_at_usage and the included-transactions check, and never changes ranking_by_monthly_fee. Welcome offers and benefits are left out and counted per product (offers_withheld, benefits_withheld, never 'none'); include=["offers","benefits"] returns them, or use list_offers and list_benefits. For one account's complete terms and rule logic use get_product_terms. A common variant of a published slug (the bank's full name, a trailing -account) answers for that product and is listed in defaults_applied.

product_slugs.description: 2 to 10 product_slugs from list_bank_products, from one or several banks.

province.description: Province: a two-letter code (ON, QC, ...) or a name such as Ontario or Québec. Default "ALL".

cohort.description: Customer group the terms apply to. Default "current" (the standard offer). Other groups a product carries (e.g. "senior_60_plus") are listed per product as variants; pass one to get that group's terms. Case and punctuation are ignored.

channel.description: How the account is opened. Default "any" (terms that apply whatever the channel).

monthly_transactions.description: Optional: the customer's typical debit transactions per month, checked against each product's included transactions.

include.description: Welcome offers and benefits are left out by default and counted per product in offers_withheld and benefits_withheld; "offers" and "benefits" return them (list_offers and list_benefits serve them across products). With offers, "clauses" adds each offer's clause ledger.

tools.name: list_offers
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which accounts have a welcome or sign-up offer, what an offer gives, or what they must do to get it. Returns each recorded offer with what you get (cash and any non-cash part, e.g. a membership), the qualifying conditions (each as a plain sentence), conditions_status, and the end date or that none is stated. conditions_status not_recorded means the conditions are unknown, never that there are none. A product with no recorded offer may still have one: say BLIA records none. Both filters are optional; omit them for every recorded offer. as_of (YYYY-MM-DD) lists the offers in force on a past date, superseded ones included. Each offer's clause ledger is left out and counted in clauses_withheld (fully_answerable and answerability already say whether the conditions are complete); include=["clauses"] returns it. Welcome offers only, which end; ongoing plan perks are in list_benefits, and fees and waiver rules in get_product_terms.

institution.description: Institution id (bmo, cibc, rbc, scotia, td: the Big 5) or a common or legal name such as BMO, RBC or Scotiabank. Omit for all.

product_class.description: Product class. Only "chequing" is covered today.

as_of.description: Optional past date, YYYY-MM-DD: the offers in force that day, superseded ones included. Omit for today's offers.

include.description: Each offer's clause ledger (every sentence of the bank's conditions text and how BLIA accounted for it) is left out and counted in clauses_withheld; include=["clauses"] returns it. fully_answerable and answerability are the same either way.

tools.name: list_benefits
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which accounts include a perk or benefit -- a credit card annual fee rebate, a safe deposit box, free drafts or cheques, rewards points, a borrowing rate discount. With benefit set, returns includes / does_not_include / not_recorded across products; without it, every tracked benefit per product. not_recorded is unknown, never 'not included'. A benefit with basis 'bank_default' is the bank's standard terms for all accounts (no product-specific benefit recorded): say so rather than calling it a feature of the plan. An unknown benefit name returns an error listing the benefits BLIA tracks. Ongoing perks only; welcome offers are in list_offers, and fees and waiver rules in get_product_terms.

benefit.description: One benefit, e.g. safe_deposit_box, credit_card_annual_fee_rebate, bank_drafts. Omit for every benefit BLIA tracks.

institution.description: Institution id (bmo, cibc, rbc, scotia, td: the Big 5) or a common or legal name such as BMO, RBC or Scotiabank. Omit for all.

product_class.description: Product class. Only "chequing" is covered today.

cohort.description: Customer group the terms apply to. Default "current" (the standard offer). Other groups a product carries (e.g. "senior_60_plus") are listed per product as variants; pass one to get that group's terms. Case and punctuation are ignored.

province.description: Province: a two-letter code or a name such as Ontario. A benefit priced differently in that province is answered with its price there. Default "ALL".

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: Use this when the user (or an app) asks what changed at the banks since a date: fee or term changes, changes a bank has announced for a future date, and welcome offers that started or ended. One call covers every bank in coverage. since (YYYY-MM-DD, at most 90 days back) is required. Each row carries the change only (before and after value, date and whether the bank stated it); for a product's full terms use get_product_terms, for an offer's conditions list_offers. BLIA's own corrections are not listed; a term with no earlier record is a first record, counted in first_records_not_listed; a change BLIA recorded after its date may fall before your window, so poll with overlapping windows. include=["summary"] adds one plain sentence per row (describes only; never advice). Open preview: see preview.ends.

since.description: Required. YYYY-MM-DD, at most 90 days back: changes dated on or after it.

institution.description: Institution id as listed in coverage.institutions_covered (bmo, cibc, rbc, scotia, td: the Big 5); a common or legal name such as BMO, RBC, Scotiabank or Royal Bank of Canada also resolves. Omit for all.

product_class.description: Product class. Only "chequing" is covered today.

kinds.description: Which kinds of change to list. Omit for all four.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a prior call with the same window

include.description: include=["summary"] adds to each row one sentence written by BLIA's code from the same logic as its rule summaries (summary_source generated_from_logic): before and after, and the date as the bank stated it or as BLIA first recorded it. Without it the rows are unchanged.
